Observations & Corrective Actions

10: 5-205.11(A) A handwashing facility shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for employee use. Pg. 163

16: 4-602.11(E)(1) Surfaces contacting non-time/temperature controlled for safety foods such as ice bins, beverage dispensing nozzles, ice makers, and coffee bean grinders shall be cleaned at a frequency specified by the manufacturer or as often as necessary to preclude accumulation of soil or mold. Pg. 145 Equipment food-contact surfaces and utensils shall be clean to sight and touch. Pg. 142

22: 3-501.16(A)(2) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control, and during hot holding, a time/temperature control for safety food (TCS) shall be maintained at 41°F or less to limit microbial growth and prevent foodborne illness. Pg. 95

23: 3-501.17(C) Refrigerated, ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety(TCS) food prepared in a food establishment and held for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the food shall be consumed on the premises, sold, or discarded. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1 and held at 41°F or less for a maximum of 7 days. Pg. 96

28: 7-102.11 Working containers used for storing poisonous or toxic materials such as cleaners and sanitizers taken from bulk supplies shall be clearly and individually identified with the common name of the material. Pg. 195

33: 3-501.15(A) Cool foods using one or more of the following methods to prevent foodborne illness: placing foods in shallow pans, separating food into smaller or thinner portions, using rapid cooling equipment, stirring the food in a container while placed in a ice water bath, using containers that facilitate heat transfer, add ice as an ingredient or other effective methods. Pg. 94-95

35: 3-501.13(A-D) TCS food shall be thawed under refrigeration at 41 °F or less, completely submerged under cool (70°F or below) running & draining water; or as part of a cooking process. Pg. 93

38: 6-202.15(A) Outer openings of a food establishment shall be protected against the entry of insects and rodents by filling or closing holes and other gaps along floors, walls, and ceilings, having closed, tight-fitting windows and solid, self-closing, tight-fitting doors. Pg. 182

39: 3-305.11 Food shall be protected from contamination by storing the food in a clean, dry location, where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination, and at least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor. Pg. 80

41: 3-304.14(B) Cloths in-use for wiping surfaces in contact with raw animal foods shall be kept separate from cloths used for other purposes. Pg. 77

43: 3-304.12 During pauses in food preparation or dispensing, food preparation and dispensing utensils shall be stored: in the food with their handles above the top of the food and container; in non-TCS food with their handles above the top of the product within containers or equipment that can be closed, such as bins of sugar; on a cleaned and sanitized portion of the food preparation table or cooking equipment; in running water of sufficient velocity to flush particulates to the drain, if used with moist food such as ice cream; in a clean, protected location if the utensils, such as ice scoops, are used only with a food that is non-TCS; or in a container of water at 135°F or above. Pg. 76-77

45: 4-903.11(A) Single-service and single-use articles shall be stored in a clean, dry location, 6" above the floor, and kept in the original protective package or stored protected from contamination until used. Pg. 153

47: 4-501.12 Cutting surfaces such as cutting blocks or boards that are subject to scratching and scoring shall be resurfaced if they can no longer be effectively cleaned and sanitized, or discarded if they are not capable of being resurfaced. Pg. 135 All equipment and utensils shall be constructed of safe materials and maintained in good repair. Pg. 20 Materials that are used in the construction of utensils and food-contact surfaces of equipment may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to food and under normal use conditions shall be safe. Pg. 113 Nonfood-contact surfaces shall be free of unnecessary ledges, projections, and crevices, and designed and constructed to allow easy cleaning and to facilitate maintenance. Pg. 119

49: 4-602.13 Nonfood-contact surfaces of equipment must be kept free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food residue and other debris for sanitary purposes. Pg. 142

51: 5-205.15(B) A plumbing system shall be maintained in good repair. Pg. 165

53: 5-501.17 A toilet room used by females shall be provided with a covered receptacle for sanitary napkins. Pg. 173

54: 5-502.11 Refuse, recyclables, and returnables shall be removed from the premises at a frequency that will minimize objectionable odors and other conditions that attract or harbor insects and rodents. Pg. 175

55: 6-501.11 The physical facilities shall be maintained in good repair. Pg. 189

56: 6-303.11 The light intensity shall be: at least 108 lux (10 foot candles) at 30" above the floor in walk-in refrigeration units, dry food storage areas and in other areas during periods of cleaning; at least 215 lux (20 food candles) where food is provided for consumer self-service, inside equipment such as reach-in refrigerators, and at 30" above the floor in areas used for handwashing, warewashing, equipment, utensil storage, and in toilet rooms; and at least 540 lux (50 foot candles) at a surface where a food employee is working with food, utensils, or equipment such as knives or grinders where employee safety is a factor. Pg. 186
